1.why: The interface uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height in the body text, although letter spacing appears standard rather than explicitly expanded.

2.why: No italics, all-caps instructions, or dense paragraphs appear on any screen; headings and labels are short and in title case.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with large text that maps cleanly to phone width, though only desktop-sized screenshots were provided.

4.why: Each screen's instruction is one or two short plain-language sentences, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone.'

5.why: The phone field shows an example format via the '+447700900000' placeholder, but the verification-code field shows no sample of the expected six-digit input.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is two sentences, so the user is never forced to read a long block to proceed.

7.why: The code had to be typed by hand ('123456' in the field) and no copy button or selectable code text is offered anywhere in the observed flow.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears in any of the five screenshots.

9.why: The inputs are plain text fields with no visible autocomplete or one-time-code affordances, so nothing indicates autofill or password-manager support for the codes.

10.why: The 'Step X of 3' label, bold heading, and full-width high-contrast primary button make the current step and primary action stand out clearly.

11.why: Each screen asks for a single primary action (Continue or Verify and continue), with only a low-emphasis 'Use different details' alternative.

12.why: After continuing, the next screen plainly states a code was sent to the phone, and after failure a banner states the request failed and to try again, although the explanation is vague.

13.why: The form permits resubmission after the error and offers 'Use different details', but there is no resend, reveal, or hide control for the code.

14.why: The banner 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming but never states what the actual problem was or how to correct it.

15.why: No reading time limit is imposed and the stated 10-minute code expiry is generous, though it remains a fixed limit on code entry.
